Prepare one row per estimated dog from the 2024 NYC licenses. Keep the recorded name beside the spelling used for matching and report missing names separately.

## Packages and helpers
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
source("R/helpers.R")
```

## From licenses to estimated dogs
### Read the license records
NYC supplies the column headers. We read ZIP codes as text because a leading zero is part of the code and matters when joining to the income data. `na = character()` keeps the city’s missing-name labels as text until we count and exclude them. This includes the two letters `NA`.
```{r}
#| label: read-license-records
sources <- read_csv("data/sources.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
dogs_raw <- read_csv(
  "data/raw/nyc-dogs-2024.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
  na = character(), trim_ws = FALSE
)
```

### Give the original license fields clear names
Give every city field a consistent `original_` name. This source table preserves the recorded values. After excluding unnamed licenses, we select the working fields with short names. The source row number lets us find the original record later.
```{r}
#| label: name-license-columns
dogs_raw |>
  rename(
    original_name = animalname,
    original_sex = animalgender,
    original_birth_year = animalbirth,
    original_breed = breedname,
    original_zipcode = zipcode,
    original_license_issue_date = licenseissueddate,
    original_license_expiry_date = licenseexpireddate,
    original_extract_year = extract_year
  ) |>
  mutate(source_row_id = row_number()) ->
  dogs_original
```

```{r}
#| label: preview-original-licenses
dogs_original |>
  preview()
```

### Missing-name labels
These are the six recorded values we agreed mean a missing name. `c()` combines them into a character vector, a sequence of text values.
```{r}
#| label: missing-name-labels
missing_name_labels <- c(
  "UNKNOWN", "NAME NOT PROVIDED", "NONE", "NA", ".", "NONAME"
)
```

### Count missing names
`pull(original_name)` takes the recorded-name column from the license table. `is.element(missing_name_labels)` checks each value against our list. The result, `name_missing`, is a TRUE/FALSE vector in the same row order as `dogs_original`. Use it to count the excluded labels.
```{r}
#| label: report-missing-names
dogs_original |>
  pull(original_name) |>
  is.element(missing_name_labels) ->
  name_missing

dogs_original |>
  filter(name_missing) |>
  count(original_name, name = "source_license_records", sort = TRUE) ->
  missing_name_counts

```

For each ZIP, count all licenses and how many lack a name. `format_zipcodes()` supplies leading zeros for digit-only ZIPs up to five digits, using the same rule as the named dogs later. `sum()` counts TRUE results. Dividing that count by all licenses gives the missing-name share.
```{r}
#| label: summarize-missingness-by-zip
dogs_original |>
  group_by(extract_year = original_extract_year, zipcode = format_zipcodes(original_zipcode)) |>
  summarise(
    source_license_records = n(),
    missing_name_records = sum(is.element(original_name, missing_name_labels)),
    named_license_records = source_license_records - missing_name_records,
    missing_name_share = missing_name_records / source_license_records,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(extract_year = as.integer(extract_year)) |>
  arrange(zipcode) ->
  missing_by_zip

```

### Keep the named licenses
`filter()` keeps rows whose condition is TRUE. `!name_missing` reverses the named result above, so we keep licenses that have names. Apply this vector to the same `dogs_original` table and row order. Select short working names here. Keep the original name and ZIP for the spelling and padding comparisons. Only named licenses continue through formatting, dates, quality flags and grouping.
```{r}
#| label: keep-named-licenses
dogs_original |>
  filter(!name_missing) |>
  select(
    source_row_id,
    original_name,
    original_zipcode,
    sex = original_sex,
    birth_year = original_birth_year,
    breed = original_breed,
    license_issue_date = original_license_issue_date,
    license_expiry_date = original_license_expiry_date,
    extract_year = original_extract_year
  ) ->
  named_licenses
```

### Format names for matching
Uppercase the whole name, then remove spaces and hyphens. These are the spelling differences we agreed to ignore when matching. For example, `WALL-E` becomes `WALLE`. Keep the recorded name during preparation so we can identify names containing spaces or hyphens before those characters disappear. We also count how many recorded spellings each estimated dog combines.
```{r}
#| label: format-names
named_licenses |>
  mutate(name = str_to_upper(original_name, locale = "en")) |>
  mutate(name = str_remove_all(name, "[\\s-]")) ->
  dogs_with_matching_names
```

### Format ZIP codes
Use the same ZIP formatting function as the missingness summary. Compare the recorded ZIP with the formatted value to count how many licenses needed leading zeros in the cleaning report.
```{r}
#| label: format-zipcodes
dogs_with_matching_names |>
  mutate(zipcode = format_zipcodes(original_zipcode)) ->
  dogs_with_zipcodes
```

### Read license dates
The source dates include a time. Take the first ten characters, such as `2024-05-30`, and read them as dates so we can sort the licenses.
```{r}
#| label: read-license-dates
dogs_with_zipcodes |>
  mutate(
    license_issue_date = str_sub(license_issue_date, 1, 10),
    license_expiry_date = str_sub(license_expiry_date, 1, 10)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    license_issue_date = parse_date(license_issue_date),
    license_expiry_date = parse_date(license_expiry_date),
    extract_year = as.integer(extract_year)
  ) ->
  dogs_with_dates

dogs_with_dates |>
  select(original_name, name, original_zipcode, zipcode, license_issue_date) |>
  preview()
```

### Flag uncertain fields
We flag compounds using the spelling on the license. We also mark records with an unknown breed or sex, a questionable birth year or a ZIP that cannot be written as five digits. These licenses still count.

```{r}
#| label: flag-uncertain-fields
dogs_with_dates |>
  mutate(
    breed_label = str_trim(breed),
    birth_year_number = as.integer(birth_year)
  ) |>
  mutate(breed_label = str_to_upper(breed_label)) |>
  mutate(
    compound_name = str_detect(original_name, "\\S\\s+\\S|[^\\s-]-[^\\s-]"),
    zipcode_padded = zipcode != original_zipcode,
    zipcode_invalid = !str_detect(zipcode, "^[0-9]{5}$"),
    breed_unknown = breed_label %in% c("", "UNKNOWN"),
    birth_year_has_four_digits = str_detect(birth_year, "^[0-9]{4}$"),
    birth_year_in_range = between(birth_year_number, 1990L, 2024L),
    birth_year_suspect = !birth_year_has_four_digits | !birth_year_in_range,
    birth_year_suspect = replace_na(birth_year_suspect, TRUE),
    sex_unknown = !sex %in% c("F", "M")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    identity_uncertain = breed_unknown | birth_year_suspect | sex_unknown | zipcode_invalid
  ) ->
  dogs_with_quality_flags
```

### Estimate individual dogs
We treat licenses with the same full name after formatting, sex, birth year, breed and ZIP as one estimated dog. Within each group, we sort the newest issue date first. A tie goes to the later expiry date, then to the earlier row in the source file. `slice_head(n = 1)` keeps the first license in each sorted group. `license_record_count` records how many licenses that row represents. For example, the two matching TOTORO licenses were issued in 2019 and 2024. The 2024 row represents both.

```{r}
#| label: estimate-individual-dogs
dog_key <- c("name", "sex", "birth_year", "breed", "zipcode")
dogs_with_quality_flags |>
  group_by(name, sex, birth_year, breed, zipcode) |>
  mutate(
    license_record_count = n(),
    original_name_variants = n_distinct(original_name),
    any_compound_name = any(compound_name),
    latest_issue_date = max(license_issue_date),
    latest_issue_ties = sum(license_issue_date == latest_issue_date)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(license_issue_date), desc(license_expiry_date), source_row_id, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    retained_row_label = str_pad(source_row_id, width = 6, pad = "0"),
    estimated_dog_id = str_c("dog2024-", retained_row_label)
  ) |>
  arrange(source_row_id) ->
  dogs_estimated
```

```{r}
#| label: estimate-individual-dogs-preview
dogs_estimated |>
  select(estimated_dog_id, original_name, license_record_count) |>
  preview()
```

### Keep the dog fields
Pass the working fields to analysis. The original name and ZIP have served their preparation comparisons. The source row number links each dog to all recorded values.
```{r}
#| label: select-dog-fields
dogs_estimated |>
  select(
    estimated_dog_id, source_row_id, extract_year, name,
    sex, birth_year, breed, zipcode,
    license_issue_date, license_expiry_date, license_record_count,
    original_name_variants, latest_issue_ties, compound_name, any_compound_name,
    breed_unknown, birth_year_suspect, sex_unknown, zipcode_invalid,
    identity_uncertain
  ) ->
  dogs
```

### Trace source records to dogs
Map the named licenses to their retained dog row. List every original row in the audit, including the excluded licenses, so the result can be traced back to the source.
```{r}
#| label: trace-source-records-to-dogs
dogs |>
  select(all_of(dog_key), estimated_dog_id, retained_source_row_id = source_row_id) ->
  dog_identity_lookup

dogs_with_quality_flags |>
  left_join(dog_identity_lookup, by = dog_key) |>
  select(source_row_id, estimated_dog_id, retained_source_row_id) ->
  named_license_mapping

dogs_original |>
  select(source_row_id) |>
  left_join(named_license_mapping, by = "source_row_id") |>
  mutate(
    record_status = case_when(
      is.na(estimated_dog_id) ~ "missing_name",
      source_row_id == retained_source_row_id ~ "retained",
      TRUE ~ "consolidated"
    )
  ) ->
  license_to_dog
```

## Cleaning summary
### Excluded names
```{r}
#| label: report-excluded-names
missing_name_counts

missing_by_zip |>
  summarise(
    source_license_records = sum(source_license_records),
    missing_name_records = sum(missing_name_records),
    missing_name_share = missing_name_records / source_license_records
  )
```

### Corrections and unresolved fields
The padded-ZIP count records corrections already made. Count it from the preparation tables; the exported dog tables need only the formatted ZIP. Unknown breeds and suspect birth years remain unresolved because the source does not provide a reliable replacement. Compound names follow the full-name matching rule. These counts describe the named licenses and estimated dogs.

```{r}
#| label: summarize-quality-flags
quality_flags <- c("breed_unknown", "birth_year_suspect", "sex_unknown",
  "zipcode_padded", "zipcode_invalid", "identity_uncertain", "compound_name")
dogs_with_quality_flags |>
  summarise(across(all_of(quality_flags), sum)) |>
  mutate(unit = "named_license_record") ->
  license_quality_counts

dogs_estimated |>
  summarise(across(all_of(quality_flags), sum)) |>
  mutate(unit = "estimated_dog") ->
  dog_quality_counts

license_quality_counts |>
  bind_rows(dog_quality_counts) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(quality_flags), names_to = "flag", values_to = "count") |>
  select(unit, flag, count) ->
  quality_summary
```

```{r}
#| label: summarize-quality-flags-preview
quality_summary
```

## Save the prepared dogs
```{r}
#| label: save-dogs
# Create the folder for these tables if needed.
dir.create("data/derived", showWarnings = FALSE)
write_csv(dogs, "data/derived/dogs_prepared_2024.csv", na = "")
write_csv(license_to_dog, "data/derived/license_to_dog.csv", na = "")
write_csv(missing_by_zip, "data/derived/missing_names_by_zip.csv", na = "")
write_csv(missing_name_counts, "data/derived/missing_name_labels.csv", na = "")
write_csv(quality_summary, "data/derived/quality_flags.csv", na = "")
```

Different dogs can share all five identifying fields. A change in a dog’s recorded details can also split its licenses into several groups. These are estimates of individual dogs.
